newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND COACH REPORTEDLY FACING SACK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND COACH REPORTEDLY FACING SACK.

text.p: Ireland's rugby union coach Murray Kidd is expected to be dismissed after the side's 37-29 mauling at the hands of lowly Italy on Saturday, Irish media said on Monday.
The Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) was not immediately available for comment on the reports, which said that the dismissal of New Zealander Kidd would be confirmed this week.
The Irish Times rugby correspondent, Edmund Van Esbeck, told Irish Radio that Kidd's departure was vital.
"It's unfortunate but it is in his own best interests and in the interests of Irish rugby," he said.
Since the start of last year's international championship, Ireland have lost six of seven matches under Kidd, including an embarrassing 40-25 defeat by Western Samoa.
Team manager Pat Whelan said after Satuday's game: "Ireland's play is devoid of any concerted or discernible pattern."
The Italians' victory strengthened pressure for their inclusion in the Five Nations tournament.
Ireland came bottom in the Five Nations tournament last year and scored only one win, a 30-17 victory over Wales.
They lost 10-16 to Scotland, 10-45 to France and 15-28 to England.
Kidd's situation was discussed at a routine post-match IRFU meeting on Sunday at which all aspects of the game were reviewed, IRFU officials said.
Kidd acknowledged that his string of defeats had created pressure for himself and the side but ruled out resigning.
"I accept that there is a lot of pressure, that's the nature of the job. But as regards me considering resigning - not in the least," he said after the game.
He said the side had a "lot of resilience" and could bounce back from the Italian humilation.
A new coach is expected to be named in time for Ireland's opening game in the 1997 Five Nations campaign against France in Dublin in two weeks' time.
All Black Mike Brewer, who coaches the Blackrock College side in Dublin, is one name which has been linked to the job as well as Dave Haslett, currently coach to the Irish "A" team.
Kidd, a succesful club coach with Garryowen and Sunday's Well, became Irish coach in 1995. Under him, Ireland have won three internationals and lost six.
